note: The (fault, expression) pairs the instruments in build/critic_suspects.py cannot see: a test that fires because of what the elevation GENERATOR does not model, stated in the generator's own source, rather than because of what the house is. Being here does not make the fault wrong; it forbids build/revise.py from sending a generator to fix it, and obliges the report to argue the case. Every entry quotes where the generator says so of itself, and build/check_critic_suspects.py verifies the quote against the file it names. WP-14.3 gives an entry a SECOND and stronger power, and gates it on a stronger warrant: an entry that also cites an OPEN question naming this fault (`question`, with `question_why` arguing it) takes its fatal findings out of `disqualified` -- the finding is still emitted, at fatal severity, with its figure, and only the verdict stops reading it. An entry with no `question` keeps the move block and does NOT excuse a disqualification, which is why the field is optional and the absence means something. A basis says the generator admits it; a question says the corpus has taken a position on it, and removing a disqualification needs both.
